basic_info.name: Starmirror (Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst)
basic_info.location: KW Institute for Contemporary Art, Berlin (31 October 2025 - 18 January 2026); K21 Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen, Dusseldorf (27 June - 11 October 2026)

practice_description.medium: AI installation, sound, sculpture, live choral AI training, image generation, performance
practice_description.practice_summary: A large-scale exhibition proposing a scenario in which AI models coordinate humans to generate intelligence for collective benefit. Transforms KW Berlin into 'part cathedral, part data center,' staging encounters between human and artificial intelligences through a machine-learning reinterpretation of Hildegard von Bingen's Ordo Virtutum (1151).
practice_description.methodology: The exhibition centres on reinterpreting Hildegard von Bingen's 12th-century morality play Ordo Virtutum as an AI training dataset, re-coding a historical text about virtue and temptation into a living vocal intelligence. Public Diffusion, a foundation image model, was trained entirely on public domain data. On select Sundays, the KW hall transforms into a recording studio where choirs, ensembles, and visitors contribute voices in call-and-response sessions, building a public choral dataset for a Berlin AI choir that will debut at K21 Dusseldorf. The project extends the Data Trust and collective governance frameworks developed in The Call.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Starmirror extends protocol art into speculative infrastructure, demonstrating how AI models can serve as coordination protocols for collective creative production. Its Public Diffusion model (trained on public domain data) and live participatory training sessions exemplify art-as-substrate that is continuously shaped by relational inputs.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes. Multiple substrate layers: Public Diffusion generates images from public domain training data; the choral AI models generate vocal compositions; The Hearth transforms GPU infrastructure into sound. Each layer can function as generative ground material.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes. The work explicitly positions AI as a coordination protocol -- a structure through which humans relate and produce collectively. The Ordo Virtutum reinterpretation maps a 12th-century relational drama (virtues vs. temptation) onto AI training architectures.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Yes. The work evolves through live Sunday training sessions where new voices are incorporated into the AI models. The Berlin choral dataset grows throughout the exhibition period, producing an evolving model that will debut in Dusseldorf.

works.title: Ur-Hildegard Training Corpus
works.description: Machine-learning reinterpretation of Hildegard von Bingen's Ordo Virtutum (1151), where the 12th-century play becomes a training dataset re-coded into a living vocal intelligence.
works.relevance: Demonstrates how historical cultural material can be re-encoded as AI training data -- treating cultural heritage as substrate for generative intelligence.

works.title: Public Diffusion
works.description: A foundation image model created by the artists trained entirely on public domain data, presented in the Arboretum section of the exhibition.
works.relevance: A commons-based alternative to proprietary image generation models. Directly relevant to A(DAI)'s commons-first orientation.

works.title: The Hearth
works.description: Acoustic organ driven by GPU cooling fans, transforming heat and noise -- byproducts of AI computation -- into an art object. Previously shown at Serpentine in The Call.
works.relevance: Infrastructure made visible and aesthetic. The material conditions of AI production become the artwork.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Starmirror is protocol art at its most ambitious. It proposes that AI models are coordination protocols -- structures through which humans organize collective intelligence. The artists approach protocols as a creative medium, designing systems (recording protocols, data trusts, training pipelines, public domain image models) that rehearse new arrangements between humans and AI. If Hildegard von Bingen was concerned with angelic orders, Herndon and Dryhurst are concerned with the hierarchies of technical protocols.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Public Diffusion (public domain foundation image model), a Berlin choral AI training pipeline with participatory Sunday sessions, and governance structures extending the Data Trust model from The Call. The exhibition itself functions as infrastructure for producing a new public choral dataset.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Strongly commons-oriented. Public Diffusion is trained entirely on public domain data, offering a commons alternative to proprietary image models. The choral dataset is being built through consented participatory sessions with governance rights for contributors. The project extends the Data Trust framework from The Call.

governance_model.governance_detail: Extends the collective governance model from The Call. Choir participants and visitors who contribute voices during Sunday sessions participate in a Data Trust framework governing how the resulting dataset and AI models are used. The Berlin choral dataset will be governed collectively by its contributors.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Participatory consent through deliberate recording sessions. Visitors who join Sunday training sessions knowingly contribute to a shared dataset governed by collective structures. Builds on Herndon/Dryhurst's extensive consent infrastructure work (Spawning, Have I Been Trained, Kudurru).
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Collaborative and distributed. Herndon and Dryhurst are lead artists, but the work explicitly credits and empowers contributing choirs, ensembles, and visitors as co-creators through governance mechanisms.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: The exhibition actively grows through live Sunday recording sessions where new voices are incorporated into the AI models. The Berlin choral dataset expands throughout the exhibition at KW, and the resulting model debuts at K21 Dusseldorf -- the work literally migrates and evolves between venues.

data_materiality.data_sources: Public domain visual data (for Public Diffusion), live choral recordings from Berlin choirs and visitor participants, Hildegard von Bingen's Ordo Virtutum (1151) as source text/training corpus, Sacred Harp hymn recordings carried forward from The Call.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Ethical and consented. Public Diffusion uses exclusively public domain data. Choral recordings are gathered through participatory sessions with explicit consent and Data Trust governance. The Ordo Virtutum source material is 12th-century public domain.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Public Diffusion operates in learned latent spaces of public domain visual culture. The choral AI models navigate latent vocal spaces. The work positions these embedding spaces as 'mirrors' -- reflecting collective human creativity back through AI coordination.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes. The exhibition spans audio (choral AI, Hearth), visual (Public Diffusion image generation, Arboretum), and sculptural/spatial modalities in a unified conceptual framework.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: KW Berlin transformed into 'part cathedral, part data center.' Multiple interconnected spaces: Arboretum with Public Diffusion, the main hall with Ur-Hildegard Training Corpus and The Hearth, and Sunday recording sessions transforming the space into a live studio. The architecture of the institution becomes the architecture of the AI training process.

interoperability.composability: Public Diffusion is a foundation model that could be integrated into other systems. The choral dataset being built is designed to be a shared resource. The recording protocol and Data Trust framework are replicable methodologies for other projects.
interoperability.technical_openness: Hybrid. Public Diffusion is built on public domain data suggesting openness. The choral dataset governance is determined collectively by contributors through the Data Trust.

technical_approach.stack: Custom choral AI models (extending Choral Diffusion from The Call), Public Diffusion (foundation image model trained on public domain data), GPU cooling fan acoustic organ, multi-channel recording systems, live AI training infrastructure

network_position.scene_affiliation: Berlin art/technology scene, KW Institute institutional ecosystem, AI art, protocol art, commons/data governance, European institutional art circuit (KW Berlin, K21 Dusseldorf)
network_position.connections: The Call (Serpentine, predecessor project), KW Institute for Contemporary Art (host institution), K21 Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen (second venue), Fellowship.xyz (gallery representing Herndon/Dryhurst), Serpentine Arts Technologies (prior collaborator), Kulturstiftung des Bundes (funder), Stability AI, IRCAM

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Starmirror extends the protocol art and collective intelligence frameworks most relevant to A(DAI). Public Diffusion demonstrates a commons-based foundation model. The live participatory training sessions model how A(DAI) might engage communities in building shared intelligence infrastructure. The project's speculative infrastructure -- AI models as coordination protocols -- is conceptually aligned with A(DAI)'s mission.
